checked.claim: Play and Stop the track run on whichever GM presses them; a non-primary GM's Stop the track during the body's silence gives the held music back and nothing re-silences it
checked.why: Traced both halves. playTrack and resetMusic gate on game.user.isGM alone and the Sound window calls them directly (no bridge, no socket in the music family). On a non-primary GM resetMusic has no record and its own `silenced` is null; with nothing playing during the silence it takes every HELD playlist (the silence's holdEverything wrote the flag in pausePlaylist) and resumes it, then schedule() returns at enabled() because that GM is not the primary. On the primary nothing wakes: watchManualPlayback returns for a sound of a mapped playlist (ours()), watchManualEnd fires only on playing:false, and no updatePlaylist handler anywhere in scripts/ calls schedule or refreshMusic (grep: the only other updatePlaylist listeners are the murder room hold, music-play.mjs:258, the Sound window's keepLive and the HUD). The primary keeps playingState bodyFound and silenced set, so apply returns at its same-state check until the state moves. The first half also holds and is worse than written: the primary's own onManualStart records held [] (the pauses landed first), so a later state change clears none of the assistant's holds, and the assistant's stale record then gives the afternoon back over the new state's music on its next Stop the track (held from the record skips the anythingPlaying guard). One nuance: the same non-primary GM pressing Stop the track after its own Play does give the music back, from its own record; what fails is the primary's side and the sidebar stop. No test drives either button from a second GM (grep of scripts/tests*.mjs: only a markup check and a tooltip row).

checked.claim: A GM who becomes the primary adopts no running cue or silence, so its next apply starts the new state's playlist under a cue still on repeat
checked.why: adoptRunningInterruption is called once, from Hooks.once("ready"), and returns at once while enabled() is false (the GM is not the primary then). No hook in the music family, sound-panel.mjs or murder-music.mjs listens for the primary changing (grep: drpgPrimaryReady and userConnected appear only in vote, passages, mastermind, incident-store). On the new primary interrupted and silenced are null and playingState is null, so the next state change reaches crossfade, which stops only ours() plus a map change's leftovers and never the cue playlist (dropCueMappings keeps it out of the map; isCuePlaylist is excluded even from `left`). The cue was set to repeat by playTrack, so it plays on. The comment above adoptRunningInterruption names 'they hand over to the other GM' as a case it was written for; it covers that only when the other GM loads after the hand-over.

checked.claim: With Music follows the game state off, a cue stopped from Foundry's Playlists sidebar leaves the music Play paused paused and flagged
checked.why: playTrack does its own holding whatever the switch says (holdEverything at 1132, record at 1142-1148). The only roads back for a cue stopped outside the module's own button are watchManualEnd and onManualEnd, both reached through hooks that open with `if (!enabled()) return` (1008, 934); resumeAmbient has no other caller, and resumeHeld is reached otherwise only from apply (also behind enabled()) and resetMusic. musicEnabled defaults to false and its onChange only calls refreshMusic. The text beside the button promises the music back on a stop; its Polish twin says the same ('Wylacz go, a wroci poprzednia muzyka'). Severity kept: the GM can press play on the ambient in the same sidebar, so this is a particular situation, not a broken session.

checked.claim: A floating text field under the case map's zoom is drawn with the unscaled font, padding and borders in the screen-sized (scaled) box
checked.why: lift() copies FACE (font-size, line-height, padding, border widths, radius) from getComputedStyle, which an ancestor's CSS transform does not change, and places the field in the top layer at getBoundingClientRect's box, which the transform does change; nothing in float-text.mjs scales the face (grep for scale, zoom: only the comments and holdSize, which sizes the placeholder alone). The case map's node editors are textareas inside the canvas that cameraTransform scales (case-view.mjs:271), and audit/float-sweep.mjs I7 measures exactly that capture at 0.5 and 2 but reads widths, the placeholder and moved siblings, never the font. By CSS semantics the floating text is drawn at 1x in a box of zoom x width. Class S only: not run in Chromium here.

checked.claim: openPlayerSoundDialog is opened by no control a player can press; only game.drpg.soundDialog reaches it
checked.why: openSoundDialog's callers in scripts/ outside the tests: gm-panel.mjs:207 (the GM panel's tile, GM only) and api.mjs:1543-1544 (soundDialog, musicDialog). No keybinding registers it (the three keybindings are toggleMute, safeword, noticeHistory). The corner launcher opens openLookDialog. So a player reaches the window by the console alone. A dead window rather than a dead control: hygiene, not a defect a player meets.

checked.ref: Sound window, GM / Effects tab Test (hints_for_other_passes.dead_controls 2)
checked.claim: Test's 'refused' answer (DRPG.Sound.why.refused) is a text no press can show
checked.why: fire(key, true) has one more road to false that the hint did not name: AudioHelper.play throwing synchronously lands in fire's own catch, which reports the file and returns false, and testSfx then shows why.refused. checked.claim: The Music slider shows Foundry's playlist volume read at open, and a change in Foundry's own Playlists sidebar is not drawn
